name: Yale Linus Smart Lock L2 (UK)

radios.note: Yale's UK page lists built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth; its UK Matter page says the lock uses Wi-Fi for Matter, not Thread.

matter.note: Matter comes by firmware update. CSA lists the Linus Smart Lock L2 (Wi-Fi and Bluetooth); the listing does not name the UK model code (SL 103).

apple_home.note: Listed on Yale UK's Matter page. Set the lock up in the Yale Home app first, then enable Matter under External Platform.

home_assistant.note: Yale's platform FAQ doesn't list Home Assistant, but its Matter page names it as the Matter hub that currently offers separate Unlock and Open Door actions.

hubRequired.note: Built-in Wi-Fi, so no Yale bridge is needed for app control; Yale's Matter page says no extra accessory is needed. The box includes a Yale Dot, which the page does not call a requirement.

localControl.note: No Yale source states local-only control.

lockFit.note: Yale says it may fit over an existing Euro/DIN cylinder, and the UK box includes a thumbturn adapter. Some doors need a new cylinder; Yale has a fit checker.

keypad.note: No keypad on the lock; Yale says PIN access needs the separate Yale Smart Keypad.

power.note: Yale's global brochure describes a Li-ion pack charged over USB-C; the UK FAQ gives up to 6 months per charge but does not name the battery type.

summary: Yale sells the Linus Smart Lock L2 in the UK as model SL 103. It fits over an existing Euro cylinder and has Wi-Fi and Bluetooth built in, so the Yale Home app works remotely without a bridge. Matter over Wi-Fi covers Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and SmartThings, and Home Assistant works through Matter. The lock has no keypad of its own.
caveats: Matter needs a firmware update on the lock, and the lock must be set up in the Yale Home app first.
Some doors need a new cylinder; check Yale's fit checker before buying.
PIN access needs the separate Yale Smart Keypad.
Battery life is up to about 6 months, and the UK pages don't name the battery type.
